purpose: Teach: せり/右下/団員/シャフト/本拠地/在り/ハイライト/ロケーション

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、市場の、絶対、せり、絶対、よく、絶対、見に行ったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When I was young, I used to go watch the market auctions all the time. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Warm nostalgic opening. Voice settles into a gentle reverie. Soft pace, unhurried. The question at the end is genuine, seeking her co-memory rather than confirmation.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。昔の絵、本気で、絶対、右下に、絶対、サイン、絶対、入っているわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Mm-hmm. Those old paintings — they always had a signature in the bottom corner, remember? You know that.
lines.style: Soft agreement with her own memory surfacing alongside his. Gentle, knowing. Slight lift on the signature detail — the recognition of a shared visual memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、町内会の、絶対、団員、絶対、お父さん、絶対、頑張ったぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When I was young, I remember Dad working so hard with the neighborhood theater troupe. You were there, weren't you?
lines.style: Voice carries both pride and a son's quiet gratitude. Steady pace. Slight hesitation before 'Dad' — the weight of saying his name to her. Seeking her version of the story.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、シャフトの加工、絶対、職人だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, your grandfather was such a craftsman — the way he'd work with those metal shafts. I can still see it.
lines.style: Voice touches tenderness. Not wistful — more present, as if she's watching it happen again. Slow, almost reverent. The detail about his craft is offered like a small gift.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 創業時、本気で、絶対、本拠地、絶対、家の隣だったぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Back when the company was starting out, the headquarters was right next to our house. You remember that?
lines.style: Light surprise in the voice — the smallness of it, how close it all was. Conversational but grounded. Pride underneath, that it began right there.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃんの、絶対、在りし日の、絶対、姿、絶対、忘れないわよ、あなた
lines.en: I never forget the way your grandfather looked in those days — so full of life. That I will always remember.
lines.style: Quiet certainty. No doubt in this statement. Voice is steady and sure, like she's making a promise to herself and to him. Slight emphasis on 'always' — not sentimental, just true.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、結婚式の、絶対、ハイライト、絶対、ばあさんの笑顔、絶対、だったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: You know what made our wedding day perfect? Your smile. That's what I remember most.
lines.style: Voice opens with warmth and softens into tenderness. Pace slows on 'your smile' — savoring the memory. Slight breathiness, like he's still moved by it. Trailing-off suggests he could say more but doesn't need to.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 新婚旅行の、本気で、絶対、ロケーション、絶対、絶景だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で、絶対、思い出
lines.en: That honeymoon — the place we went was just breathtaking, wasn't it? I still hold that memory close.
lines.style: Wistful but grounded. Voice has a light, almost weightless quality when she speaks the location — vivid and present. Closes with quiet certainty. Unhurried breathing, like she's letting herself linger in it.
